Whereas in the earlier regulations of 1956 and 1963 a general sanction by the association was the withdrawal of a license to participate, in 1968 the sanctions were differentiated, ranging from a ban of one month for the first doping offense up to a lifetime ban when an athlete tested positively four times.  The change from vague doping controls external to the athlete's body, like food and drink, to substances inside the body marks a paradigm shift. Controls no longer stop outside the body, so to speak. With some respect, controls of an athlete's body include the violation of his bodily integrity. This change is reminiscent of Michel Foucault
